content.question: What is the key difference between top-k and nucleus (top-p) sampling?
options: Top-k always samples from exactly k tokens, while top-p samples from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p, so the candidate set adapts to the distribution's shape
Top-k works only with greedy decoding, while top-p works only with beam search
Top-k increases entropy, while top-p always reduces the vocabulary to a single token
Top-p samples only from the k most probable tokens, while top-k uses a probability threshold
content.answer: Top-k always samples from exactly k tokens, while top-p samples from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p, so the candidate set adapts to the distribution's shape
